newsitem.title: USA: Coors specialty brew to go nationwide.
newsitem.headline: Coors specialty brew to go nationwide.

text.p: Adolph Coors Co's specialty label Blue Moon beers will be available nationwide by February 1, up from 45 states currently, a Coors executive said on Thursday.

Last September Golden, Colorado-based Coors Brewing Co in a bid to capture a share of the growing, pricier specialty beer market, launched four Blue Moon beers in 22 markets. Besides Belgian White Ale, Honey Blonde Ale, Nut Brown Ale and Raspberry Cream Ale, there is also a seasonal beer, Harvest Pumpkin, sold in the fall.
Jim Sabia, brand manager for the Blue Moon label, said the Blue Moon specialty beers are less "hoppy" than other microbrews on the market.
"It's as complex as any specialty beer out there, but there's a balance between hops and malt," he told a news briefing.

He said the Blue Moon label was "not as esoteric" as other specialty brews. The specialty beer market has grown 40 to 50 percent in the past four or five years, Sabia said, although the segment remains tiny at about two-to-three percent of the national market.
Sabia declined to say what percentage Blue Moon represents of all Coors beers sold, other than to say it was "very small."
The traditional beer market - young men in the 20s - has not been growing, presenting brewing companies with a challenge to find ways to enlarge the pie.
